summary.name: Postgres.app
summary.one_liner: Postgres.app is a full-featured PostgreSQL installation packaged as a standard Mac app with a menu bar item and one-click server setup.
use_cases: Running a local PostgreSQL server on a Mac without the command line
Developing applications against a local PostgreSQL database
Geo data work with PostGIS on macOS
Connecting Python, Ruby, Go, Java or C applications to a local Postgres server
summary.what_it_does: Packages a full PostgreSQL installation as a standard Mac app, including the PostGIS extension. It offers a menu bar item and a user interface for creating and running a server, and it can be used without touching the command line. It ships the psql client, command line tools and header files for advanced users. The page gives setup steps (move to Applications, click Initialize, optionally set PATH) and default connection settings of localhost, port 5432, no password. It also includes example connection code for PHP, Go, Python, Ruby, Java, C and Swift, and notes that minor updates can be installed automatically.
notable: Full PostgreSQL bundled as a standard Mac app with PostGIS included
Menu bar item and GUI for managing the server, no command line required
Bundled psql, command line tools and libpq headers for Swift/C development
Automatic installation of minor PostgreSQL updates
caveats: Some features may not work unless the app is in the Applications folder
Instructions assume no prior PostgreSQL installation; other installs (Homebrew, MacPorts, EnterpriseDB) should be removed first
The system-provided PHP on macOS does not support PostgreSQL; the page recommends MAMP
The system libpq on macOS does not support SSL
